lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write a multiply sentence and a related divide sentence for: 9 rows of 6 chairs.

FEEDBACK
9 × 6 = 54 chairs; 54 ÷ 9 = 6 (or 54 ÷ 6 = 9).

WATCH FOR
Choosing multiply for a sharing question reverses the story.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Solve fourteen multiply/divide word problems. Label equal groups / array / sharing for each and show the number sentence.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

Parent: Likely misconception: Choosing multiply for a sharing question reverses the story. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses word problem with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Equal groups: 8 bags of 12 oranges → 8 × 12 = 96. Sharing: 96 oranges into 8 bags → 96 ÷ 8 = 12. Same numbers, different questions.

TRY FIRST
Write a multiply sentence and a related divide sentence for: 9 rows of 6 chairs.

FEEDBACK
9 × 6 = 54 chairs; 54 ÷ 9 = 6 (or 54 ÷ 6 = 9).
teach_steps.explain:
Multiplication and division word problems need a model of equal groups, arrays or sharing before calculating.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Choosing multiply for a sharing question reverses the story. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
teach_steps.title: Understand and model
